settings.title: The Importance of Double-Glazed Glass Washing Machines
settings.text:
UPVC double-glazed doors and windows are among the best options for insulation against heat, noise, and pollution.
One of the essential factors in achieving this insulation is the use of double-glazed glass, which plays an important role in window performance.
Today, double-glazed glass is manufactured in dedicated workshops using specialized machinery.
An essential piece of equipment found in double-glazed glass manufacturing plants is the industrial glass washing machine.
As you know, double- or multi-glazed glass consists of glass panes separated by aluminium spacers. Inert gases such as argon, and sometimes krypton, are injected into these spacers.
This raises an important question: how is the glass properly cleaned during production so that the final product is delivered completely clean and free of stains?
Are operators responsible for manually cleaning the glass with detergents? Certainly not.
Specialized double-glazed glass washing machines are used to achieve the best possible results.

settings.title: How an Industrial Glass Washing Machine Works
settings.text:
An industrial glass washing machine is essential for the production of double- and multi-glazed glass. Without it, the final product quality would be significantly reduced.
The process begins when the first pane of the double-glazed unit enters the washing machine from the production line.
Inside the machine, the glass is thoroughly washed by pressurized water and rotating brushes, then transferred to the drying section.
In the drying section, all glass surfaces are exposed to hot air, which completely dries the glass.
After drying, the glass moves to the inspection section.
There, it is placed on a panel where the operator uses fluorescent and incandescent lighting to identify and correct any defects.
If defects such as stains are found, the glass is returned to the washing section for another cleaning cycle. Once approved by the operator, it proceeds to the next stage.
The glass is then transferred to the pressing machine, where it waits for the second pane.
The second pane follows the same process: it enters the washing machine, passes through the dryer, and, after operator approval, is placed on the spacer alignment section so that the spacer can be fitted in its position.
It is worth noting that throughout the industrial washing and drying stages, no manual handling or hand-operated tools are involved.
By contrast, in non-industrial and manual production processes, these operations are performed by hand using very basic tools. As a result, lint, stains, scratches, and other defects can be seen inside the glass unit.

These machines are available in vertical and horizontal configurations and are usually manufactured with different numbers of brushes, which directly affect washing quality.
Typically, horizontal machines are 3.5 to 4 metres long, while vertical machines are 6 to 8 metres long. The width of a horizontal washing machine and the length of a vertical washing machine can also be customized.
